articles.title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang loses $7.4bn in 30 minutes, drops 2 spots in Forbes rich list
articles.summary: Nvidia's CEO Jensen Huang faced a notable drop in net worth, tumbling from $162.2 billion to $154.7 billion, following revelations of an ongoing investigation into his supposed involvement with a Chinese spy. The resulting unrest caused Nvidia's shares to plunge by more than 7%, raising alarms about its market stability as broader questions emerge regarding Nokia's dealings in China and their national security ramifications.

articles.title: US evacuates aircraft from UK air base after Iran threat: Report
Bus driver burnt alive as arson attacks, crude bomb blasts rock Bangladesh
articles.summary: A 60-year-old bus driver was killed in an arson attack on a parked bus in Faridpur. Multiple incidents of vehicle arson and crude bomb explosions were reported across various districts in Bangladesh. The Dhaka Metropolitan Police increased security and arrested 19 individuals linked to these attacks. Investigations are underway to determine those responsible for the violence.

articles.title: Hegseth unfazed by impeachment push, defends Trump's Iran war as 'necessary'
What Nvidia CEO first told world about the woman he has admitted having an affair with
articles.summary: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang publicly acknowledged an affair that has raised concerns over his leadership. Following his admission, Nvidia initiated an independent investigation into reports concerning foreign intelligence involvement. Huang expressed remorse for his actions towards his family and colleagues while committing to cooperate with the inquiry. US President Donald Trump commented on the situation, stating that the FBI is investigating the matter.

articles.title: 3 contract workers drown during tank cleaning at Tata facility in Tamil Nadu
articles.summary: Three contract workers tragically drowned while cleaning inside a feed tank at Tata Marigold Company. The deceased, identified as Kaveri, J Akmal, and Sarath Kumar, were all from Rayakottai. They were rescued and taken to a nearby hospital, where they were pronounced dead. Authorities have initiated an inquiry to investigate the circumstances surrounding this incident. Law enforcement will monitor the facility to maintain order during this investigation.

articles.title: Ohio truck driver leads push to block proposed $5bn Amazon data centre
articles.summary: Residents in Butler County are rallying against the proposed Amazon data center, voicing worries over possible water shortages, noise pollution, and pollution from backup generators. Local zoning authorities have suggested prohibiting data centers in St. Clair Township, where this project is slated to occur. A crucial public hearing is set to address these issues alongside zoning matters. Recent trends show rising voter favor for restrictions on similar undertakings across Ohio.

articles.title: 'Injured throat with scissors': Kolkata techie's girlfriend 'can't remember' argument
articles.summary: Sarthak Sarkar, a software engineer, was found murdered in his rental flat in Kolkata after a domestic dispute. His live-in partner, Sanchalika Basu, and her mother, Moumita Basu, have been arrested in connection with the case. Investigators are examining conflicting statements provided by the arrested women regarding the circumstances of Sarkar's death. The couple reportedly argued over allegations of extramarital affairs shortly before the incident occurred.

articles.title: China hits $1 trillion trade surplus milestone for second year in a row
articles.summary: China's trade surplus surpassed $1 trillion in the first ten months, driven primarily by high-tech product demand. Exports increased significantly due to the global AI investment boom, although imports also grew faster than expected. Domestic consumption remains weak, which has pressured manufacturers to seek overseas markets for growth. Trade tensions with the European Union and the United States add complexity to China's export situation.

articles.title: New Jersey teen, 16, turns potato peels and coffee grounds into weedkiller
articles.summary: At just 16 years old, Leo Toake from New Jersey is on a mission to create a revolutionary herbicide sourced from food scraps. Through his nonprofit, Re:Imagine Inc., he's mobilized over 70 volunteers for habitat restoration and invasive species removal. Early trials of Toake's S.A.F.E. clearly show an 82.5% effectiveness against Japanese stilt grass, all while repurposing over 500 pounds of food waste and contributing to a cleaner environment.

articles.title: Utah family keeps disputed farmland strip after neighbour's survey challenge
articles.summary: A Utah family successfully upheld its legal rights to a disputed piece of farmland after a court ruling. The Christiansen Family Trust contested boundary claims made by Haas Land & Livestock, which purchased neighboring property. The property dispute centered around a fence built in 1965 that marked the boundary. The Utah Court of Appeals affirmed earlier decisions favoring the Christiansens' long-accepted boundary.

articles.title: Russia-US diesel deal delivers results? Lavrov claims prices have already fallen
articles.summary: Russian foreign minister Sergei Lavrov stated that an agreement allows Russia to resume diesel exports to the US. The arrangement aims to stabilize energy markets and improve energy security amid rising fuel prices. Ukrainian attacks on Russian energy infrastructure continue, impacting fuel shortages in several regions of Russia. Despite concerns over regulatory issues, the US Treasury Department confirmed compliance with legal standards for the deal.

articles.title: Iran war, cost of living drag Trump’s approval rating near career low: Survey
articles.summary: Donald Trump's approval rating stands at 32 per cent, close to his lowest in recent years. Concerns about the cost of living have significantly affected his standing among voters. The Republican Party experienced losses in both chambers of Congress during the midterm elections. Trump has taken action to address immigration, which resonates more positively with his supporters compared to his economic policies.

articles.title: Donna Kelce opens up about the challenges of keeping up with her sons' busy careers
articles.summary: Travis Kelce’s mother, Donna Kelce, opens up about how their careers have made their lives challenging.

articles.title: Patrick and Brittany Mahomes' $1.4 billion KC Current project faces funding backlash
articles.summary: Patrick Mahomes and Brittany Mahomes' KC Current stadium expansion has advanced despite opposition from three Kansas City council members. The proposed $185 million public funding agreement would increase CPKC Stadium's capacity to 18,000 seats. Concerns remain over limited development details, redirected tax revenue and the project's benefits for residents. Despite the objections, the council approved the agreement.

articles.title: Tezpur University helps solve 60-year chemistry mystery
articles.summary: Researchers from Assam's Tezpur University have contributed to an international chemistry breakthrough, helping scientists isolate stable oxoboranes for the first time. The discovery, published in Nature Chemistry, resolves a challenge that chemists have pursued for more than 60 years. Led by Professor Ashwini K. Phukan, the Indian team provided computational support to researchers at Germany's University of Würzburg, who successfully produced three oxoboranes through reactions involving diboracumulene and ketones.

articles.title: Why Shubman Gill is captaining India for the last time in ODI series
articles.summary: Shubman Gill leads India in his final match of the ODI series against New Zealand at Seddon Park. He will miss the fourth and fifth ODIs due to workload management before the Test series. India are ahead in the series, leading series 2-0. Shreyas Iyer will take over as captain for the final two matches.

articles.title: Charlie Kirk murder trial set for June 2028 as judge rejects defence's push for 2029
articles.summary: Tyler Robinson, implicated in the assassination of Charlie Kirk, will begin trial in June 2028. The judge aimed to balance the interests of both the defense and Kirk's widow, Erika Kirk. Prosecutors originally sought an earlier trial start, highlighting the family's desire for swift justice. Robinson's lawyers are preparing a substantial defense, examining extensive evidence and potentially seeking a change of venue.

articles.title: 4 lakh guests, 150 dishes: Anant Singh's goes all out for daughter's wedding
articles.summary: Anant Singh is organizing an elaborate wedding for his daughter in Ladma village on November 25. The event will showcase a luxury Land Rover Defender and a BMW for family members. Horse racing will also occur, with substantial prizes for the winners to attract participants from multiple states. A wide variety of food dishes will be served, totaling over 150 options.

articles.title: X locks TOI photojournalist's account after smog posts
articles.summary: Amidst rising air quality concerns, Anindya Chattopadhyay, a dedicated photographer, found himself at the center of a storm when his X account faced a lock due to smog images taken around NH9 and Lodhi Garden after Diwali. Committed to truth-telling through his lens, Chattopadhyay was undeterred by the backlash, with the Delhi government refuting any involvement in this controversial decision.

articles.title: 'Global capital for Sanatan': Akhilesh's big Ayodhya promise ahead of UP polls

He stressed the importance of honest temple management and top-notch infrastructure to rejuvenate devotees' trust. articles.title: Booker Prize 2026: 81-year-old M John Harrison becomes oldest-ever winner
articles.summary: M. John Harrison won the Booker Prize at the age of 81 for his novel 'The End of Everything'. The win marks a significant achievement for science fiction within literary circles, making him a pioneering figure. His novel is set in a dystopian future following a mysterious catastrophe affecting society. Harrison's past works and contributions to the genre have set the stage for this victory.

articles.title: Stock market today: Check if NSE, BSE are open or closed for Diwali-Balipratipada
articles.summary: With the festive season bringing changes to the regular trading calendar, investors may be wondering whether the stock market will remain open or closed today, Tuesday, November 10. Following a special Muhurat trading session on Sunday and a regular session on Monday, both the BSE and NSE will remain closed today on account of Diwali-Balipratipada. Regular trading will resume on Wednesday, November 11.

articles.title: India's chess GMs: 100 and counting – Why becoming a GM is now just a tiny step

While reaching the Grandmaster title is commendable, certain players manipulate rules to safeguard their ratings. Currently, only a few maintain an Elo rating above 2500, exposing the fierce competition. The ongoing scarcity of sponsorship and support for chess talents is a pressing issue, which contrasts sharply with better-resourced nations.

articles.title: Diwali as US federal holiday? 19 lawmakers back fresh push
articles.summary: A group of Indian-American lawmakers supports legislation to establish Diwali as a federal holiday in the United States. Congresswoman Grace Meng leads the initiative alongside 14 other representatives advocating for the recognition of Diwali. This legislation aims to promote cultural awareness and inclusion among diverse communities. The festival represents significant values across various religious groups and cultures, uniting people.

articles.title: ‘In the dark’: NCP MLAs seek clarity as merger buzz creates confusion
articles.summary: Confusion has arisen within the Nationalist Congress Party regarding possible merger discussions among its factions. While NCP leaders have privately acknowledged the exploration of merger options, official communications remain unclear. Following the death of Ajit Pawar, merger talks have reportedly stalled, causing discontent among party members. Party leaders are expected to address concerns and further discuss merger possibilities after the Diwali festival.

An assailant fatally attacked a special SI while he was attempting to disperse a group of unruly youths. In a separate incident, an IT technician was stabbed after an argument over debris from firecrackers. The police have arrested several suspects in both cases to address these violent incidents.

articles.title: Pawan Kalyan and wife Anna Konidela announce separation

They expressed mutual respect and a continued commitment to their children’s well-being in a joint statement. Pawan Kalyan and Anna married in September 2013, and they have a daughter and a son together. Pawan previously married actress Renu Desai and has two children with her as well.

articles.title: 'No intention to attack Europe': Russia rejects fears of military confrontation

He criticized Western discussions about military conflict as unfounded and stressed the need for dialogue. The ongoing Russia-Ukraine negotiations are set to resume soon with both sides preparing for talks. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy emphasized that his country will not concede territory during the discussions.

articles.title: 'You always have the gun to your head': Ravi Shastri on life as India head coach

articles.title: Delhi pollution mystery: 36 monitoring stations 'go offline' as smoke engulfs Capital
articles.summary: This Diwali, Delhi faced its highest air pollution levels in five years, sparking doubts about the accuracy of monitoring systems. Numerous air quality stations ceased reporting at critical times, creating gaps in data. In contrast, private monitoring agencies discovered far greater pollution levels than the government reported, prompting accusations of data manipulation. Reliable air quality information is vital for ensuring public health, especially during pollution crises.

An independent investigation has been launched by Nvidia's board regarding the claims. Huang has also admitted to personal issues but maintains no national security breaches occurred.

articles.title: Four businessmen back $29m loan tied to Ponzi scheme; bank wins no damages

This initiative will see the assembly of the ARAD 5 rifle and NEGEV UX machine gun taking place in Tilburg. articles.title: Finland pours 100m gallons of water into giant pit to store heat for homes
articles.summary: Hyvinkaa is embarking on an ambitious project to fill an old gravel pit with 100 million gallons of water, designed for thermal energy storage. This facility is set to provide approximately 25% of the city's heating requirements during the colder months. While construction is scheduled to continue until late April 2027, the facility is expected to start charging by late summer 2027.

articles.title: North Dakota son loses $100-an-acre farmland deal after failing farm condition

articles.title: Blackouts and no heating: Russia’s winter strike campaign takes aim at Ukraine’s energy network
articles.summary: Russia has commenced a significant campaign of missile and drone strikes against Ukraine's energy facilities, leading to power outages. Ukrainian officials reported large-scale damage in multiple regions, leaving many without electricity or heating. Ukraine is responding by targeting Russian missile launch sites to diminish their capabilities. Despite Ukrainian efforts, Russian forces continue their offensive operations, and logistics remain a hurdle for them.

Her return is likely to heighten the existing political unrest and may further complicate India-Bangladesh relations, as discussions on her extradition unfold.

Firecracker usage persisted beyond permitted times despite restrictions, worsening pollution levels. The Air Quality Early Warning System forecasts that unhealthy air quality conditions may continue in the coming days.

The escape raises concerns about the enclosure’s security and the challenges of containing a wild tigress. Previously, this tigress had also escaped within days of her initial release in October.

articles.title: Rejected a job offer for chess, now he's India's 100th GM: How Anuj Shrivatri made it

His journey, which began in childhood under the influence of his father's fascination with chess, had seen multiple unsuccessful attempts before this triumph. As he celebrates this remarkable milestone, Shrivatri is committed to honing his skills and aims to dominate in more chess tournaments.

Washington seeks to regulate Iran's nuclear capabilities and ensure access to the Strait of Hormuz. Iran demands the lifting of sanctions and recognition of its strategic interests in any agreement. Despite diplomatic efforts, significant divisions remain regarding nuclear concessions and economic relief. Both sides face internal pressures complicating the path to a resolution.

Nvidia's board has initiated an independent investigation into reports of a foreign intelligence operation. The investigation involves Alice Huang, a former executive accused of being linked to China's Ministry of State Security.

Tragic incidents have occurred where individuals and families reportedly ended their lives amid mounting debt pressures. In various regions, police are investigating alleged harassment by moneylenders and recovery agents involved in these cases. The emotional pain and traumatic experiences from debt repayments have left families devastated and grieving.

articles.title: 'Slipped, suffered heart attack': B'luru woman, her lover arrested for killing husband

After initially claiming he suffered a heart attack, police investigations revealed Upendra died of asphyxiation. The couple had frequent arguments about Anita's relationship with Madhusudhan, which escalated the night before the murder. Evidence suggests that Madhusudhan assaulted Upendra while Anita helped to suffocate him.

This marks the fourth police encounter since the BJP assumed power in West Bengal in May.

articles.title: ‘They have stopped hoping’: Inside Manipur’s deepening mental health crisis

An estimated one in eight individuals faces mental illness, with suicides rising among displaced families. Sanitation issues and inadequate living conditions affect both children and adults, exacerbating their trauma. Displacement has shattered families, with many experiencing deep loss and bereavement. As hope diminishes, communities are left to grapple with a bleak future.

articles.title: 'A party invitation': How Bengaluru family was massacred inside house

After the initial murder of Sunita, he allegedly invited his brothers-in-law to his home, where he killed them as well. The investigation revealed that he used a grinding stone for the killings and then attempted to clean the crime scene. A missing-person report prompted police to discover the situation and arrest Indushekar.

articles.title: Microsoft data centre site in Amsterdam 'attacked'
articles.summary: On November 6, protestors stormed a Microsoft data centre construction site near Amsterdam, raising concerns about power usage. The activist group Geef Tegengas argues that the centre will strain local electricity supplies significantly. Police initially sought to block the demonstration but were overwhelmed as protesters broke through barriers. Previous protests have targeted the same location, reflecting escalating frustrations about technology infrastructure.

The court also rejected his claims of breach of contract and bad faith against Safeco Insurance.

After shining at Borussia Dortmund, Jobe's selection underscores his rapid ascent, while Cole Palmer and Phil Foden remain sidelined due to injuries.

articles.title: Kenyan cult leader gets 200 years for starving 190 children to death
articles.summary: Paul Nthenge Mackenzie faces a staggering 200-year prison sentence for orchestrating the Shakahola massacre, which tragically claimed the lives of numerous church members, including 190 innocent children who reportedly starved under his directives. He manipulated his followers to believe that fasting would bring them closer to Jesus in the face of an impending apocalypse.

articles.title: Watch: Karmabhoomi Express coaches gutted in Punjab; short-circuit suspected
articles.summary: A fire erupted in three coaches of the Karmabhoomi Express in Patiala district, Punjab on Friday around 1pm. The sudden flames instilled fear in passengers as they spread quickly. Promptly, railway officials and emergency teams arrived to manage the situation, which was likely caused by a short circuit. Fortunately, all passengers were unharmed, and alternative transportation was arranged for their continued journey.

articles.title: Boy starts food bank at 9 with £40; six sites now help 5,000 people yearly

Isaac's mother highlights the positive community response and the inspiration his actions have sparked in others.

articles.title: Georgia O'Keeffe painting bought for $3,800 could now fetch up to $3m

With its auction set for November 18, a public exhibition will showcase the artwork at Rockefeller Center in early November.

However, evidence, including surveillance footage and forensic analysis, contradicts his account, revealing blood linked to Kafle. Despite the grave allegations, Bhatt asserts his innocence and pleads not guilty.

articles.title: China's helicopter arsenal grows, is India ready for the Himalayan challenge?

The People's Liberation Army's investments could shift military balance along the Himalayan frontier against India. India, in response, is strengthening its own helicopter fleet with various indigenous and foreign platforms. Both nations are prioritizing aerial mobility for effective operations in challenging mountainous terrain. The ongoing developments highlight the evolving military dynamics between India and China.

articles.title: Bomb threat to Amitabh Bachchan's bungalow, Bombay HC, BSE on Dhanteras

Authorities are currently investigating the credibility of the threat and determining appropriate actions. Further details about this situation are expected shortly from official sources.

articles.title: 2026 set to be second-hottest year ever recorded; El Nino yet to peak
articles.summary: The year 2026 is anticipated to be one of the warmest on record as global temperatures soar. Experts suggest that the prevailing El Niño will peak around this time, intensifying the risk of severe weather phenomena worldwide. The World Meteorological Organization warns of impending droughts and floods as a result, while projections hint that temperatures might rise even more in 2027, threatening existing climate balances.

The incident occurred at their rented house in Palavakkam, resulting in Muthupriya suffering ten stab wounds. After the murder, he left their daughter with his brother in Mudichur. Family members revealed Vivek had a history of mental health issues and had received treatment recently.

Relatives Kantharaju and Manjappa were arrested for attacking her over property disagreements. Police found clues suggesting that the murder was premeditated rather than a robbery gone wrong. Both suspects have confessed to their roles and remain in police custody.

Commuters faced delays on key roads, with some journey times stretching to nearly two hours. Cab fares saw a considerable increase due to high demand and restrictions on certain vehicles entering the city. Many commuters expressed their frustration regarding the traffic situation and rising transportation costs on social media.

articles.title: OBC creamy layer row: SC protects past jobs, promotions; leaves pending cases open
articles.summary: The Supreme Court has clarified that its March ruling will not impact completed appointments or promotions. Cases still pending will be examined individually by the courts based on merit and eligibility. The government expressed concerns that retrospective application could unsettle established positions and admissions. It sought two years to establish a uniform creamy layer mechanism across various sectors.

He aims to reclaim essential military aid while stressing the immediate necessity for Patriot air defense missiles and the operational readiness of F-16 fighter jets as winter approaches.

articles.title: Pakistan's external debt nearly doubles to $135 bn in 10 years, China biggest lender
articles.summary: Pakistan's external borrowing is projected to reach $135.1 billion by 2025, with much of the debt owed to China. The country's external debt increased from $68.673 billion in 2015 to the current level, reflecting a significant upward trend. Public and publicly-guaranteed borrowing comprises the majority of this debt, totaling around $107.076 billion. Private borrowing is notably more expensive, contributing to rising debt-service payments across developing countries.

articles.title: 2nd-gen Gujaratis script history in US midterms
articles.summary: Seven Indian-American candidates achieved victories in the US midterm elections, marking a significant milestone for the community. Ami Bera won in California’s 6th Congressional District, securing his position as the longest-serving Congressman of Indian origin. However, the enduring executive powers from the Trump era pose challenges for immediate reforms. articles.summary: Cristiano Ronaldo has officially retired from international duty with Portugal after 23 years and six World Cups. He announced his retirement through an emotional video message to the Portuguese people, marking the end of his national career. Ronaldo holds a record of 146 international goals and significant victories, including Euro 2016 and the UEFA Nations League title.

articles.title: Bombay HC cancels Sachin Waze's bail in Antilia bomb scare case
articles.summary: The Bombay High Court has overturned the bail originally granted to Sachin Waze regarding the serious Antilia bomb scare incident. This move came after the National Investigation Agency appealed against the previous bail decision. Waze, arrested in March 2021, remains in custody as the court highlights explosive elements and security threats, raising crucial legal and investigative discussions surrounding the case.

articles.title: Jeff Bezos' ex-wife $30 mn donation gets 10 yr affordable housing plan in Bay Area
articles.summary: Housing Trust Silicon Valley has unveiled an ambitious 10-year initiative aimed at improving affordable housing in the Bay Area. With a generous $30 million backing from MacKenzie Scott, this plan seeks to bolster homeownership initiatives and forge stronger alliances with policy advocacy. The focus is on maximizing current funding and attracting new resources to create and maintain affordable housing for the community over the next decade.

articles.title: Drones carrying drones: Turkey turns Bayraktar TB2 into flying weapons carrier
articles.summary: In an innovative leap in drone technology, Turkey's Bayraktar TB2 is being engineered as a launch platform for smaller kamikaze drones. Recently, it showcased its capabilities by successfully deploying Skydagger FPV drones onto targets. This integration not only enhances the operational range of these attack drones but also allows the TB2 to act as a communications hub, potentially redefining strategic warfare through coordinated aerial strikes from a single unit.

articles.title: Iowa landlord loses $700k in alleged Ponzi scheme; $351k divorce award upheld
articles.summary: An Iowa landlord, asserting a $700,000 loss from a Ponzi scheme, sought to reduce his divorce payment but was unsuccessful. The Iowa Court of Appeals confirmed the trial court's $351,446 ruling. The husband contended his premarital assets should remain separate; however, the court determined these assets were commingled and part of the marital estate. This case emphasizes the necessity for clear marital property agreements.

'Why is this a special case?' Judge accused in son's deadly car crash gets bail

articles.title: Footballer's death: Goalkeeper Owono left out of Equatorial Guinea’s AFCON squad
articles.summary: Equatorial Guinea goalkeeper Jesus Owono has been excluded from the AFCON qualifiers following the death of Jesus de Miguel. De Miguel passed away after a collision with Owono during a match, leaving many in mourning. Owono expressed deep sorrow and struggles to process the tragedy he experienced. He has faced online abuse, leading him to deactivate his social media account.

Greenpeace drops nine celebrity-signed boulders to curb North Sea fishing
articles.summary: Environmental activists from Greenpeace have deployed nine limestone boulders in the Southern North Sea to prevent bottom trawling. This underwater barrier aims to protect marine biodiversity, particularly harbour porpoises affected by industrial fishing. Greenpeace argues that government protections have been insufficient to shield marine habitats from destructive fishing methods. The deployment of boulders took place without a marine licence, raising regulatory concerns.

articles.title: Tech billionaire Kenneth Hao, wife commit $175M for healthcare transformation
articles.summary: Kenneth Hao and Kathy Chiao have generously donated $175 million to the University of California system, with the aim of modernizing medical infrastructure and enhancing healthcare technology across both human and veterinary medicine. Their pledge emphasizes the necessity for innovative facilities that foster advanced medical technologies, particularly benefiting UC San Francisco and UC Davis. Through the Hao Family Foundation, they continue to focus on impactful charitable contributions.

articles.title: Ludhiana girl, 6, holds difficult yoga pose for 18 minutes, sets record
articles.summary: At just six years old, Sarah Sangar from Ludhiana has made headlines by holding the seated wide-legged yoga pose on a gymnastics balance beam for 18 minutes and 20 seconds, setting a new record. Recognized by the India Book of Records on October 3, 2026, this accomplishment not only highlights her impressive bodily control and flexibility but also encourages children everywhere to pursue excellence in physical fitness through dedicated training.

Cristiano Ronaldo announces retirement from international football
articles.summary: Cristiano Ronaldo announces his retirement from the Portuguese national team, expressing his intent to relinquish the cherished number 7 jersey following the November international fixtures. With an extraordinary record of 234 caps and 146 goals, he leaves behind a legacy as the all-time leading goal-scorer and appearance maker, concluding a remarkable era in international football.

articles.title: Ollie Watkins' wife Ellie returns to UK with kids amid Saudi security concerns
articles.summary: Ollie Watkins’ wife, Ellie, has returned to the UK with their two children months after his reported £50 million move from Aston Villa to Al-Hilal. Citing security concerns and regional conflict in Saudi Arabia, she said the family would stay in Britain until conditions improve. Watkins, meanwhile, continues his career in Riyadh, having recorded six goals and five assists in 10 appearances.

articles.title: US issues Forever stamp celebrating Diwali, features Rangoli created by Indian artist
articles.summary: In a vibrant tribute to Diwali, USPS has launched a new Forever stamp showcasing a stunning rangoli design by Sangita Bhutada. The unveiling occurred at the Embassy of India in Washington DC on October 21, marking the second issuance of a Diwali stamp since 2016. Crafted over eight to ten days with colored sand, this stamp edition comprises 20 million copies for collectors and enthusiasts alike.

articles.title: Trump's Midas curse: Why his golden picks turned blue in US midterms 2026
articles.summary: Donald Trump's endorsement of numerous candidates in the 2026 midterms proved less effective than anticipated, leading to notable electoral disappointments. Democrats triumphed in Senate and House elections, gaining ground in areas that were once Republican strongholds. The performance of Trump's endorsed candidates reflected a troubling disconnect with voters. Furthermore, Democratic success extended to gubernatorial elections and state legislatures, thereby underscoring an evolving political landscape laden with challenges for the GOP.

articles.title: Sensex settles over 2,000 points higher, investors end Rs 8 lakh cr richer: Top reasons for rally
articles.summary: Dalal Street witnessed a major surge as Sensex soared over 1,600 points and Nifty50 gained 2%. This rise in the market was supported by a decline in crude oil prices and returning foreign investor interest. The US midterm election results also contributed positively to market sentiment globally. Broader market indices and banking stocks joined in the rally, reflecting widespread investor confidence.

articles.title: Hardeep Singh Puri elected unopposed to Rajya Sabha from Madhya Pradesh
articles.summary: Hardeep Singh Puri was elected unopposed to the Rajya Sabha from Madhya Pradesh after other candidates failed to qualify. The nominations of Rajkumar Lohani and Kante Sayanna were rejected for not meeting necessary requirements. Puri's election follows the resignation of Union minister of state L Murugan in mid-October. Hemant Khandelwal, among other officials, was present when Puri collected his election certificate.

articles.title: The push for low-cost standoff weapons: Why air forces are turning to glide bombs
articles.summary: The US Air Force is investigating new glide bomb technologies to lower costs associated with missile-led campaigns. Current operations in prolonged conflicts have highlighted the expense of missile usage. The US military is also pursuing powered missile variants to enhance strike capabilities in various scenarios. India is developing similar glide bomb technologies aimed at increasing precision and operational range for its forces.

articles.title: Bombay HC shields Ananya Panday; platforms must erase AI images
articles.summary: The Bombay High Court has ordered the takedown of objectionable content violating Ananya Panday’s privacy, after she alleged businesses used her photos and AI-generated content without consent. Justice Madhav Jamdar cited her privacy and dignity rights. Meanwhile, the Delhi High Court gave Kriti Sanon limited relief, excluding news, parody and fan content.

articles.title: Smoking, bike rally, songs greet man accused of murdering 16-year-old boy

Following his release, he was welcomed with garlands outside the jail and took part in a bike rally. A viral video showed him participating while smoking a cigarette atop a vehicle during the procession. Authorities are now questioning possible violations of traffic rules and public safety during the event.

articles.title: ‘If death is my destiny’: Sheikh Hasina firm on returning to Bangladesh in December
articles.summary: Sheikh Hasina has confirmed her intention to return to Bangladesh, despite facing a death sentence. The former Prime Minister is aware of the risks associated with her return, including potential arrest or worse. Hasina's Awami League party has been banned, resulting in widespread political repression and violence against its members. She expressed concerns over the rising influence of extremist groups in the current political climate.

articles.title: Guitar mistaken for pillion, turban for bare head: When AI traffic cameras get it wrong
articles.summary: AI-powered traffic cameras are increasingly being utilized in India for automated enforcement of traffic rules. However, the technology faces significant challenges resulting in numerous erroneous challans issued to motorists. Incidents include misidentification of objects, such as guitars and turbans, as violations leading to fines. Complaints regarding the accuracy of the system have surged, highlighting accountability issues. As technology evolves, ensuring accuracy is crucial in minimizing errors encountered by drivers.

articles.title: Trump's midterm setback may ease tariff pressure on India: Report
articles.summary: The outcome of the 2026 midterm elections could significantly boost India's leverage in trade negotiations with the US. With Democrats gaining power, Trump's capacity to enforce harsh tariffs is constrained, alleviating pressure on India. This shift allows India to pursue trade agreements more strategically and carefully, potentially resulting in better deals. Furthermore, new legal constraints on Trump limit his tariff imposition options, enhancing India's prospects in upcoming trade discussions.
